content:
Let \(b\) and \(p\) be the first-day counts of buns and pears.

Buns sum:
\[
nb-\frac{n(n-1)}2=264
\]
Pears sum:
\[
np+\frac{n(n-1)}2=187
\]

Adding gives:
\[
n(b+p)=451
\]
so \(n\mid 451=11\cdot 41\).

Subtracting gives:
\[
n(b-p-n+1)=77
\]

For \(n=11\):
\[
b+p=41,\qquad b-p-10=7 \Rightarrow b-p=17
\]
so \(b=29,\ p=12\), which works.

The larger divisors \(41,451\) fail the difference condition, and \(n=1\) is degenerate.

\[
\boxed{11}
\]
